observation.observation:
**Visible tissue.** A single spheroid rendered in the "Core" tab, cutaway at z ≤ 0 µm. Two cell states are legible against the legend: violet spheres (dead tumor) dominating the bulk, and a smaller pale "pearl" (living tumor) cluster confined to the upper-left rim. Amber spindle CAFs ring the outside, none embedded in the core. The header states "57 living tumor cells · whole volume," but the cutaway shows only a partial slab, so the on-screen pearl count cannot be reconciled with 57.

**Field and legend.** The alanine bar is a fixed shared range 0 · 0.05 · 0.1 mM. Field opacity is 30%, and in the main view the field is essentially invisible — no gradient is readable around the spheroid. The inset voxel slice is a flat teal square with visible pixel blocking; its own text reads 0.0100–0.0320 mM, i.e. the data occupy roughly the bottom third of the 0–0.1 mM scale, so the fixed range compresses rather than exaggerates contrast. It also notes the slice is at z = 10.0 µm while the requested z is 0 µm — the inset does not match the cutaway plane.

**Defects.** Opacity/scale mismatch hides the field; inset z offset; dense sphere packing occludes interior cells; count label unverifiable from the visible slab.

**Spatial effect.** Only a qualitative one: living cells sit on one flank, CAFs strictly peripheral. Nothing about uptake, secretion rate, causation, or whether CAF alanine sustains tumor survival can be inferred — the condition dropdown names a setting, it does not demonstrate it.

observation.observation:
**Visible content.** Two paired panels at 1,440 min, both cutaway z ≤ 0 µm, 50 µm scale bars. Panel 01 ("CAF secretion · uptake intact") reads **57 living tumor cells · whole volume**; panel 02 ("Tumor uptake suppressed") reads **0**. Yet both spheroids look nearly identical in size and packing — dense violet (dead) spheres with orange spindle CAFs ringing the periphery. Only panel 01 shows a small cluster of pale pearl (living) cells at the upper-left rim; panel 02 shows none. So the 57-vs-0 contrast is carried by ~a dozen visible pearl beads, not by the bulk of the rendered mass.

**Nutrient field.** Both inset "Alanine · exact voxel slice" tiles are flat teal, essentially indistinguishable. Their legends read 0.0100–0.0320 mM (01) and 0.0100–0.0321 mM (02), against a fixed shared range 0–0.05–0.1 mM. Both note "0 saturated voxels." The measured spread is ~0.002 mM — far below the legend's tick spacing, so the color ramp cannot resolve any difference; the shared scale is honest but the field is effectively uninformative here.

**Concrete defects.** (1) The count "57" is not visually verifiable — pearl cells are mostly buried; violet occludes the interior at 30% field opacity. (2) Cutaway z ≤ 0 µm and voxel slice z = 10.0 µm are different planes, so field and cells are not co-located. (3) Insets are low-resolution and clipped by panel edges. (4) "whole volume" counts are compared against a single sliced view.

**Spatial effect.** Only one is visible: surviving pearl cells sit at the spheroid rim adjacent to CAFs, consistent with a peripheral-survival gradient — but it is a single asymmetric patch, not a full rim.

**Not inferable.** Whether uptake suppression caused death, any alanine flux or exchange direction, per-cell metabolic state, interior viability, time course before 1,440 min, or CAF contact dependence. This is a rendered simulation; nothing here verifies biology.
